meta.task: #595 R3 readiness-group opportunity census (read-only, no timing claim)
meta.host: E5, Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3, Fedora 44, kernel 7.2.11-200.fc44.x86_64

diagnostic_build.worktree_after_census: diagnostic bench sources reverted to baseSha; git status --porcelain empty; HEAD 0a22a791

ready_group_definition: A set of independent reads whose file, offset, length, destination buffer and dependency conditions are all determined before the first baseline submit of the set; no added wait, no moved-up dependency work, no prefetch.

primary.task: 4 KiB positional reads on a 64 MiB warm-tmpfs fixture, uring backend, external progress driver thread + submitter thread
primary.why: In steady state the consumer already consumes every front-ready completion and then refills the window in one burst. At the first submit of that burst every member's slot/offset/buffer is already fixed by the consumer's own state (window.size, submitted, depth, blocks); no member depends on another member's result and no wait occurs inside the group. 91-93% of 20k submits for d16 and 72-73% for d4 fall in multi-ready groups.

d64.note: 512-request diagnostic window; group size 64 fits one enter at queue_depth=64

split_point.visible_state: window.size()=w<depth, submitted=s, r=min(depth-w, request_count-s); for member j: slot=(s+j)%depth, offset=((s+j)%blocks)*4096, dst=buffers[slot], len=4096; source file fd already open; no completion take and no wait between group-ready and the r submits.
split_point.real_enter_difference: Baseline: r pure submit enters (each io_uring_enter to_submit=1, min_complete=0; measured 60,000 such enters per invocation = 3 phases x 20,000, i.e. 20,000 per 20k-op phase). Capacity-capped split: ceil(r/queue_depth)=1 enter because r<=depth=queue_depth; saving r-1 per group. d16: 18,202-18,669 enters saved per 20k (91.0-93.3%); d4: 14,455-14,637 (72.3-73.2%); d64 512-window: 502-504 (98.0-98.4%).
split_point.concrete_example: w03-d16-verbose phase 1 group 2: group_ready ts=5079642908035 with ready=16, window=0, submitted=16; first submit at group_ready+934 ns; members (slot,offset,len)=(0,65536,4096)..(15,126976,4096) with 16 distinct buffers; all 16 submits succeeded; group_done=16. Baseline cost 16 enters, batched 1, difference 15.
split_point.scope: Only the W-03 external-loop refill bursts under the consume-all-ready policy. Does not apply to W-02 default steady state (one ordered wait per iteration) or to sluice-copy steady state (next read depends on that slot's write completion). The batching prototype must not extend the existing completion wait to grow a batch.

shadow_screening.multi_ready_group_second_member: Already ready before the first submit; intra-group submit gaps are the existing per-submit call cost (diagnostic p50 77-92 us for d16, include verbose logging; not a wait).
shadow_screening.single_ready_group_second_arrival: Arrives only in the next refill after the existing completion wait; inter-group gap p50 201-225 us for d16 full phase 1-2, 111 us phase 3; d4 p50 136-239 us. The next read is not data-dependent on the previous result, but issuing it in the same batch would require moving or adding a wait, which is forbidden.
shadow_screening.use_limit: Shadow data only filters hypotheses; it does not show that waiting would be faster and no cross-call wait was added.

w02_pipeline.why: The default consumer waits for the oldest ticket and settles exactly one request per outer iteration, so every steady-state refill has exactly one ready member (D2: 19,998/19,998 steady groups single). Only the initial window fill has depth members. Net saving is depth-1 enters once per phase: D2 1/20,000 = 0.005%; D4 3/20,000 = 0.015%.

sluice_copy.classification: NO_REAL_BATCH_EXPOSURE at the default depth=1; STARTUP_ONLY when pipeline_depth>1
sluice_copy.why: At the default pipeline_depth=1 there is no group even at startup. For pipeline_depth>1 the prefill loop submits pipeline_depth independent reads before any wait (a startup group), but each steady-state next read depends on that slot's write completion (chunk_offset is advanced only after the write returns), so the next read is not ready at another read's first submit. Source-level conclusion; not run.

enter_baseline.interpretation: Every invocation reports 60,004 io_uring_enter: 60,000 pure submit enters (to_submit=1, min_complete=0, one per submit_read across 3 phases x 20,000) + 4 context-probe enters (to_submit=1, min_complete=1, IORING_ENTER_GETEVENTS). No enter had to_submit>1: 0 coalesced SQEs, max 1 SQE/enter, and all enters were on the submitter thread (driver thread 0). Diagnostic-on and unmarked diagnostic-build runs have identical counts; 512-request verbose traces show 1,536 pure submits + 4 probes per invocation.

checks: No wait, sleep, retry inflation or parking was added; existing waits are unchanged (W03 cv wait at :370, W02 scope.wait_for at :384).

No dependency work was moved earlier: the diagnostic only predicts/logs slot/offset/dst from state that the product already holds; it does not construct ReadOps, submit, or consume on the product's behalf.
No prefetch: the same reads are submitted at the same points; no extra read.
Only bench TUs were modified (test-only diagnostics + a census-only W02 D2/D3 case switch); libsluice_async.a is byte-identical to the frozen baseline.

limitations: No performance timing or formal A/B was run; all enter counts are syscall counts, not latency claims.

The r distribution comes from a diagnostic build. Minimal recording (one clock read + one vector push per group) reproduces the multi-ready dominance (91.1-92.9% enter saving for d16), and unmarked/frozen enter counts are identical, but the absolute r rates are workload/scheduling dependent and vary by phase.
The W03 batch opportunity is downstream of the consumer's existing completion wait; it must not be re-used to justify adding cross-call waits.

The R2 B-arm deferred-flush gate is owner-gated (submitter must be the recent progress driver); in W03 the submitter is not the driver, so the R2 prototype would not capture this group. Capturing it needs consumer-side SQE preparation batching, not a longer defer.
W02 D2/D3 cases exist only under the census-only SLUICE_CENSUS_D2 switch (the frozen baseline case list has no d2); sluice-copy was not instrumented.
The 4KiB warm-tmpfs shape and this host are the only measured scope.
